While Luke Skywalker was recovering from his injuries, Jedi Knights [[Avinoam Arelis]] and [[Sothais Saar]] in the Outer Rim were attacked by a tentacle that suddenly materialized before it disappeared; the Jedi Council believed that it was a remnant of Abeloth that targeted a representation of her hatred for the Jedi. The Jedi Council believed that Abeloth would eventually recover and return, albeit not in their lifetimes.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

Master Skywalker sent for Raynar Thul, reasoning that the Ones' deaths and Abeloth's destruction meant that there was no need to help the Killiks rebuild their hives and risk antagonizing the Chiss. Skywalker also convinced the Jedi that removing themselves from Coruscant would be in the best interests of the beleaguered capital, wishing to spare it from being caught in the crossfires of further conflict with the Sith; the Jedi would relocate to the world Shedu Maad, and acting Chief of State Wynn Dorvan would propose a Senate resolution to treat any attempt to infiltrate the Galactic Alliance as an act of open war. The Grand Master himself continued to feel the anguish of Abeloth's balled tentacles in his chest wound,<ref name="Apocalypse" /> which also cost him a [[Rib/Legends|rib]] and a part of a [[Lung/Legends|lung]].<ref name="Crucible">[[Crucible (novel)|''Crucible'']]</ref>

[[File:Jaina_et_Jag_Sakuub.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Jagged and Jaina Solo Fel investigated an ancient ruin for possible information on the Jedi or Abeloth.]]
The [[Holocron of Luke Skywalker]] documented the Jedi's struggle against Abeloth and the Sith Tribe, and in it, the Grand Master made clear that he had learned that the Jedi must devote wholly to the light side by focusing on the challenges and mysteries of their most important ally, the Force, rather than issues of galactic politics.<ref name="Warfare" /> He was troubled that the imbalance of the Force would continue to plague the galaxy, given the chaos and darkness over the past half a century.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> He also sought to understand Abeloth's origins and the nature of the Ones so that the Jedi could better follow the will of the Force and restore balance&mdash;whether that was to truly destroy Abeloth, constrain her, or to acknowledge her role in the galaxy and create a new order.<ref name="Warfare" />

To ensure the immortal Abeloth's destruction should she resurface, Skywalker sought to obtain the Dagger of Mortis as described in the Jedi Archives' Mortis report. To that end, ten young [[Quest Knights]] were dispatched throughout the galaxy in [[Hunt for Mortis|search]] of the Mortis Monolith. At the same time, the Hapes Consortium publicly announced Allana Djo Solo as the first heir to the Hapan Throne.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

During Jagged and Jaina Solo Fel's honeymoon in the same year of 44 ABY,<ref name="TERC" /> Jaina persuaded her [[Wedding of Jagged Fel and Jaina Solo|newlywed]] husband to hike on [[Sakuub]]<ref name="Getaway">{{InsiderCite|134|Getaway}}</ref>&mdash;an Outer Rim world of the [[Pelgrin sector/Legends|Pelgrin sector]]<ref name="EAOC Sakuub">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Sakuub system/Legends|Sakuub system]]</ref> that housed an ancient ruin named the [[Sky Temple of Karsol]]&mdash;where she hoped to learn whether it was a lost Jedi site or contained any information about Abeloth. The pair uncovered a [[Sakuub Holocron|Jedi holocron]] at the temple, and though they were [[Skirmish on Sakuub|attacked]] by a [[Pharika|local guide]] working for an unknown party upon the discovery, they were aided by a [[Unidentified Hutt (Sakuub)|Hutt]] and escaped with the [[Holocron/Legends|holocron]].<ref name="Getaway" />

====The wound that would not close====
[[File:MortisMonolith.png|thumb|left|300px|Despite defeating Abeloth, the Jedi Order continued searching for the Mortis Monolith (pictured) before she could return in full force.]]
A year into the search for Mortis, in [[45 ABY]],<ref name="TERC" /> the Jedi [[Ohali Soroc]] found a [[Unidentified monolith|monolith]]<ref name="Crucible" /> matching the Mortis Monolith's appearance<ref name="Overlords" /> in Wild Space's<ref name="EAOC Chiloon">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Chiloon Rift/Legends|Chiloon Rift]]</ref> [[Chiloon Rift/Legends|Chiloon Rift]]. The [[Columi/Legends|Columi]] entrepreneurs [[Craitheus Qreph|Craitheus]] and [[Marvid Qreph]] had constructed their [[Base Prime|base]] on the monolith itself, which expanded space and time around its vicinity, and wished to exploit its power. While Vestara Khai attempted to take advantage of the Qrephs' operation and enter the monolith herself together with the brothers, they predicted her betrayal and entered the monolith without the Sith, who fled with Ship.<ref name="Crucible" />

Although the Masters of the Council were worried about the mysterious wound that Abeloth had left in Luke Skywalker's chest, the Grand Master had claimed that pain only occurred when he experienced Force visions and set off for the Chiloon Rift. After dispatching the Qrephs' Mandalorian mercenaries with help from a strike team that included Ben Skywalker, Tahiri Veila, and Lando Calrissian with his latest [[YVH-8 S-series battle droid|YVH battle droids]], Luke Skywalker and Han and Leia Organa Solo followed the Qreph brothers into the structure, which contained an ethereal realm.<ref name="Crucible" />

====Every loss a step====
[[File:Crucible_Brazilian_cover_art.jpg|thumb|right|330px|Luke Skywalker, Leia Organa Solo, and Han Solo entered a mysterious monolith, but they failed to find Mortis or the dagger that could destroy Abeloth.]]
While there, the mark that Abeloth left in Skywalker's chest remained a dark void while other parts of his body shone in a luminous gold due to the raw strength of the Force. His companions also glowed in gold as they resisted the temptation of the shadows that lingered there, but the Qrephs were corrupted after accepting help from the shadows, becoming dark specks.<ref name="Crucible" />

As the Jedi, held between life and death, destroyed the Qrephs through the Force, Luke Skywalker realized that darkness and destruction were inseparable from light and life. Skywalker concluded that the monolith was imbalanced and that Mortis was not in it&mdash;at least at that time. The trio consisting of himself, Leia Organa, and Han Solo subsequently decided to retire from galactic affairs, confident that the rest of the Jedi would be able to grow beyond them.<ref name="Crucible" /> When Darth Krayt, the Sith Lord whose fate had been so linked to the Bringer of Chaos's rise and fall, led the One Sith conquest of the galaxy nearly a [[127 ABY|century later]], individuals such as the Jedi [[Cade Skywalker]],<ref name="Legacy War 6">[[Legacy — War 6|''Legacy — War'' 6]]</ref> [[Ania Solo]], and Empress [[Marasiah Fel]] worked with the Fel Empire, Jedi Order, and later the [[Galactic Federation Triumvirate]] to bring an end to the Sith hold over the galaxy.<ref name="Legacy 2013 1">[[Legacy (2013) 1|''Legacy'' (2013) 1]]</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Expandsect}}
{{Quote|This stuff grows wherever Abeloth sets up house. It's how she feeds.''"<br />"''On fungus and moss? What is she, some kind of cave-creeper?''"<br />"''Abeloth is no herbivore, Fett. She feeds on fear. Anguish. On what beings feel as they suffer and die.''"<br />"''You're telling me she feeds on ''death?"<br />"''Not in the way you mean. She feeds on the ''feelings'' death causes. Fear and pain release a lot of dark side energy. That's what Abeloth is after.|Tahiri Veila and Boba Fett|<ref name="Apocalypse" />}}
Abeloth was an entity antagonized by loneliness; she felt an absolute need to be loved and adored, and was nearly overcome when Vol attacked her with the idea that she was hideous and despised. She fed her craving for adulation by instilling in Force-sensitives a desire to be with her, and in turn catered to their every need and assumed the role as their mother. This stemmed from her original fear of losing her family, who remained ageless while she became old. In an attempt to hold on to the life she had, Abeloth drank from the Font of Power and bathed in the Pool of Knowledge, which corrupted her mind and twisted her love for her family into a craving for companionship. When her family abandoned her on their planet&mdash;the very reason she committed her crimes in the first place&mdash; she was driven insane by loneliness and despair.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> An outgrowth of this loneliness was her vulnerability to Force attacks that tore at her identity or mocked her as unlovely and doomed to be hated.<ref name="Ascension" /> 

Similar to the rhak-skuri creatures of Upekzar, she fed on the terror of her victims.<ref name="Ascension" /> She spread mass-terror by creating chaos, in an attempt to gain more power, as her ultimate goal was to recreate her lost family&mdash;she wanted Luke Skywalker to take the place of the Father, luring him by possessing Castilla Ming and Akanah, whom Skywalker loved, and tried to force Ben Skywalker and Vestara Khai to drink from the Font of Power, intending them to be the replacements for the Son and Daughter.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

While on Pydyr, Abeloth's eyes shone as she told Luke Skywalker that she had more bodies that he could kill, taking pleasure in the Jedi's distress.<ref name="Vortex" />

====To hide a smile====
When introduced to the Sith at the Kesh masquerade, Abeloth had a sweet smile.<ref name="Ascension" /> Abeloth's capacity for deception affected the Sith Lords of Kesh, the politicians of the Galactic Senate, and even the Jedi Grand Master Luke Skywalker. She subverted the democracy of the Galactic Alliance, which was already strained by the tension between Chief of State Daala and the Jedi Order, both by appealing to senators as a kindly Rokari Kem who represented a people who had long struggled against slavery and by taking advantage of the politicians who were under the payroll or otherwise manipulated by the Sith Tribe led by High Lord Workan on Coruscant.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

Abeloth was also a skilled campaign manager, promoting Grand Admiral Daala's candidacy for the Imperial leadership election against the popular reformist incumbent, Jagged Fel. Although Daala was largely supported by Imperial military commanders, Abeloth instigated a mob attack on Fel's supporters and exploited the secretive Moon Maiden facility to create propaganda material supporting Daala that Abeloth had imbued with a persuasive aura via the Force.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

===Incarnations and poses===
{{Quote|How many bodies ''do'' you have?''"<br />"''More than you can kill. I promise you that.|Luke Skywalker and Abeloth|<ref name="Vortex" />}}
Abeloth was able to shapeshift at will<ref name="Abyss" /> and possess other beings, making them avatars of her own by sharing her Force essence among multiple bodies&mdash;even the Jedi Temple's computer core. Her growing power quickly deteriorated bodies, particularly those who were not Force-sensitive, and Abeloth was weakened when one of her avatars was destroyed. Her Force essence also existed in the realm beyond shadows.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

When the Sith Tribe first made contact with her on her world, she appeared as a humanoid female of indeterminate species.<ref name="Abyss" /> When she was aboard Meliflar Station, Abeloth appeared as a slender woman with brown hair and silver eyes, donning a robe.<ref name="Conviction" />

Aside from fully absorbing other beings and taking complete control of their bodies, overriding the original individual that lived within&mdash;with the exception of Callista Ming, who had experienced living as a disembodied spirit herself and resisted Abeloth's grasp thanks to her relationship with Luke Skywalker&ndash;Abeloth was able to imbue a small part of her dark essence in another being&mdash;she did so to Fala, on Meliflar Station, to divert her Jedi pursuers,<ref name="Conviction" /> as well as Tola Annax on Upekzar.<ref name="Ascension" />

====Someone sweet and kind and fun?====
{{Quote|<nowiki />''Callista?''"<br />"''You ''could'' say that.|Luke Skywalker and Abeloth, as Callista Ming|<ref name="Vortex" />}}
[[File:Callista_Ming.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Abeloth was able to take the form of those she consumed, such as Callista Ming.]]
Abeloth was able to appear as Callista Ming after absorbing the Jedi.<ref name="Vortex" /> She could transform into both Ming's newer body, which had been donated by Cray Mingla, and Ming's original body. As Ming's original form, she had dark and thick curly hair,<ref name="Allies" /> high cheeks, a full-lipped mouth, an aquiline nose, and gray eyes.<ref name="Vortex" /> In Mingla's form, Abeloth had short honey-gold locks and slightly silvery gray eyes. Aside from gaining Luke Skywalker's recognition for her appearance as Callista Ming, Abeloth's presence was also felt by Skywalker to be an intimate one; the Jedi believed that it was the presence of the spirit of his late wife, Mara Jade, that was comforting him aboard Jade's ship, the ''Jade Shadow''.<ref name="Allies" />

====Standing hollow-eyed====
{{Quote|Her hair was long and yellow and fell all the way to the ground. Her eyes were tiny, sunk deep into black eye sockets&mdash;like two small stars. Her mouth was&mdash;it reached literally from ear to ear, and her arms were short, stunted&mdash;with writhing tentacles instead of fingers. She was hideous.|Vestara Khai, describing Abeloth's true form|<ref name="Allies" />}}
However, Abeloth's true form was that of a humanoid being with deeply sunken black eye sockets and tiny silver eyes reminiscent of tiny stars at the bottom of a deep well<ref name="Allies" /> or a black hole.<ref name="Ascension" /> She had a long cascade of straw-like, honey-blond<ref name="Allies" /> or saffron<ref name="Abyss" /> or pale yellow<ref name="Ascension" /> hair that reached to the ground and a large, full-lipped mouth that stretched from ear-to-ear and contained needle-like teeth.<ref name="Allies" /> Her arms were stubby, protruding no more than ten centimeters from her shoulders, with hands that had long, writhing tentacles for fingers with suction cup tips.<ref name="Abyss" /> Her body was rigid and straight, and when she walked or ran, her legs rippled forward more than they swung.<ref name="Allies" />

When transforming from one appearance to her true form, Abeloth changed progressively, with her mouth widening, her skin paling, her eyes sinking into their sockets, and her hair becoming longer.<ref name="Ascension" /> Abeloth's body was sometimes shrouded in mist, giving her an ethereal aspect to her already frightening appearance.<ref name="Conviction" /> Luke Skywalker saw her true form beyond shadows and Vestara Khai was able to see her true appearance after Khai discovered Abeloth's treachery against the Sith.<ref name="Abyss" />

====Catastrophic blues====
As the Jessar Rokari Kem, Abeloth maintained a sweet façade that had popular appeal among Coruscant's citizenry, including among its senators and journalists. Her face had green eyes under blue-green brows and her long, flowing hair featured shiny blue-green tresses. She spoke mellifluously and had blue skin and three fingers on each of her two hands.<ref name="Ascension" /> While contemplating the return of the Jedi on Coruscant in their repurposed temple, Abeloth wore a formal white gown.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

====Lavender face====
{{Quote|Chief Dorvan, will you please put your feet down? Or do you expect Lady Korelei to continue holding you there for the rest of the day?|Abeloth, holding Dorvan aloft while speaking from her Rokari Kem manifestation|<ref name="Apocalypse" />}}
Possessing Lady Korelei, Abeloth was a tall Keshiri who had dark lilac-colored skin that was almost as blue as Rokari Kem's. She had dark hair and lavender lips and her long oval eyes became cold and empty, except for flickers of silver in the darkness. Dorvan felt terror creeping up to him as the lavender face grew a wide smile filled with fangs.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Well, they can't simply have just disappeared. I mean&mdash;that was a lot of ships. They've got to be somewhere.''"<br />"''Physics would dictate that, but I get the feeling that Abeloth and the Sith aren't great believers in physics.|Jaina Solo and Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Ascension" />}}
{{Expandsect}}
===Sweet like honey===
{{Quote|You couldn't stop looking at her, whatever she chose to look like. It was all you wanted to do&mdash;look at her, be around her. Like an intoxicant.''"<br />"''Her looks varied, then?''"<br />"''From day to day, or depending on whomever she was around. Always more or less human though. Sometimes fair hair, sometimes brown, sometimes long, sometimes short. The features shifted, the eye color changed a little. Until &hellip; until the moment I really ''saw'' her.|Vestara Khai and Luke Skywalker, on Abeloth|<ref name="Allies" />}}
While afflicted with Abeloth's psychosis, Dyon Stadd heard the entity speaking to him within his thoughts. He felt that he knew her and did not know her at the same time, but believed that Abeloth was kind and good, a source of understanding and strength.<ref name="Allies" />

===Unlimited power===
{{Quote|I am programmed to obey a strong will. The girl is strong. You are stronger, Sword of the Jedi. But neither of you can break the hold she has on me. She is older, and more powerful than you can possibly imagine.|Ship, to Jaina Solo|<ref name="Allies" />}}
Abeloth was an astonishingly powerful Force user, such that it was deemed impossible for mortals to understand her dark power.<ref name="Abyss" /> Jaina Solo compared her to being as like a nova.<ref name="Vortex" /> She was described by [[Tahiri Veila]] as a living Force volcano.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> Ship considered Abeloth to be much stronger of will then Vestara Kahi or Jaina Solo, such that no one could command him while Abeloth ruled.<ref name="Allies" />

Abeloth could [[Plant Surge|command]] the native flora of her planet to do her bidding.<ref name="Abyss" />

She also had the ability to [[Mind trick/Legends|influence the minds]] of Force-sensitive beings who had spent an extended period of time in the Maw, causing in them a [[Force psychosis|psychosis]] which made them believe that everyone&mdash;except for other such psychotic beings&mdash;had been replaced by impostors and instilling in them a desire to find her. The afflicted Jedi, as a result of this, were granted knowledge of many new Force powers varying from person to person, such as Fold Space, Force Deception, Phase, lightning and Flow walking powers, and a technique to paralyze people.<ref name="Abyss" /> Once the influenced being found her, she [[Force drain/Legends|consumed their life energy]], tearing away their vitality with golden light, so killing them and making herself stronger. The strength of her influence was formidable&mdash;even when the Jedi learned what symptoms to look for, upon the onset of the psychosis they still believed that everyone they knew was an impostor. Abeloth [[Telepathy/Legends|called]] Ship to her from across the galaxy,<ref name="Omen" /> bidding him come to her service, and nearly was able to use her mind to deceive Luke Skywalker into using the Pool of Knowledge, reveled herself in "beautfic" psychic form to Ben Skywalker, and confounded a whole strike force of Sith to the point that all of them failed to notice how she was having them killed off, until Vestara Khai explained the threat.<ref name="Abyss" />

She was also able to control the Meditation Sphere Ship which was programmed to obey the strongest will; her powers overwhelming those of the Sith's and of the Jedi's attempts to control the Sphere.<ref name="Allies" /> Moreover, she could mind trick whole rooms of lesser beings into supporting her political statements and [[Sith alchemy/Legends|craft]] Force-imbued posters that would inspire those who looked on them to vote for Dalaa.<ref name="Ascension" /><ref name="Apocalypse" />

Abeloth's strength [[Enhance Attribute|physical augmentation]] was a dozen times that of Luke Skywalker, who was widely recognized as the most powerful Force user in the galaxy. However, Skywalker was able to defeat in a duel her despite this by raining debris on her.<ref name="Vortex" /> Abeloth was able to [[Force speed/Legends|boost her walking speed]] with the dark side, to the point that she could keep up with Sith.<ref name="Abyss" /> Additionally, she could use [[Tutaminis]], usually with ease.<ref name="Vortex" /><ref name="Apocalypse" />

Abeloth wielded exceptional [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetic powers]], using the Force to blast everyone away from her during her battle with the Sith and Jedi, choke Sith, murder the Chief of State with Force Wound, and hurl around aircraft.<ref name="Allies" /><ref name="Ascension" /><ref name="Apocalypse" /> Abeloth's sheer strength was extensive&mdash;after her [[Telepathy/Legends|mental]] duel with Vol, an utterly enraged Abeloth released waves of Force energy on Tahv that caused the beings in her vicinity to [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Crush|implode]], those farther away to be ripped to pieces, the buildings to melt to the ground, and glass and weaponry to fly through the city, looking for someone to hurt so that they could feel the pain she felt--the heat of the burning debris set much of the city on [[Fire/Legends|fire]].<ref name="Ascension" /> Abeloth was able to move people around with the Force from across star systems and lift them with ease.<ref name="Abyss" />

She was able to, with great effort, partly resist the powers of a [[control web]], and was also able to [[Fold space|teleport]] herself short distances from one place to another, a power which she also used during her battles with the Sith and Jedi.<ref name="Allies" /><ref name="Apocalypse" /> Abeloth had the most powerful use of [[Force healing/Legends|Force Healing]] that Luke Skywalker had ever encountered.<ref name="Conviction" /> Abeloth was able to take on the physical appearances of beings that she had consumed, including Callista Ming and Dyon Stadd, and she was also able to project images of other beings, as she did when projecting an image of Callista while she herself took on the form of Stadd in an attempt to trick Luke Skywalker.<ref name="Allies" /> Abeloth was able to [[Force deflection/Legends|redirect]] Vestara Khai's [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] back at her. She was also more than capable of using Force lightning herself, using it in multiple fights with the Sith and Luke Skywalker.<ref name="Apocalypse" /><ref name="Allies" /> She was known to feed on fear and death.<ref name="Apocalypse" /><ref name="Vortex" /> She was also capable of compressing a huge amount of Dark Side power and using it to detonate a volcano.<ref name="Ascension" /> She was alleged to know [[Sever Force/Legends|Sever Force]].<ref name="Ascension" /> Abeloth occasionally used Force Flight.<ref name="Ascension" /><ref name="Apocalypse" /> She possessed some skill at a variant of [[Cryokinesis]], chilling living matter (such as Sith) as desired, as well as [[Pyrokinesis]] and could [[Tutaminis|deactivate]] lightsabers from a distance.<ref name="Abyss" /><ref name="Apocalypse" />

Abeloth was also able to [[Essence transfer|possess or switch]] bodies&mdash;before Skywalker could kill her, she switched bodies with Stadd and took on Stadd's appearance, tricking the Jedi and Sith for several days into believing that she was dead. Later, she took over the body of the Fallanassi Akanah Norand Goss Pell, although Pell fought back. When she was again defeated by Skywalker, she left Pell's body and returned in the form of Callista soon after, and told Skywalker that she had more bodies than he could destroy.<ref name="Vortex" /> She was also capable of absorbing the consciousness of beings in order to enhance her power further, as Callista Ming's mind dwelled within Abeloth. However, Luke was able to use a dark side variant of [[mnemotherapy]] to rip Callista Ming's soul free from Abeloth and allow her to rest in peace, severely weakening Abeloth in the process.<ref name="Conviction" /> She was later able to use her abilities to impersonate Rokari Kem and gain prominence on Coruscant. When Vol attempted to assassinate Kem, she [[Sai cha/Legends|beheaded]] the Grand Lord and forced High Lord Ivaar Workan to aide her in becoming Chief of State of the Galactic Alliance.<ref name="Ascension" /> Later, she also possessed Imperial Officer [[Lydea Pagorski]], as part of a plan to help [[Natasi Daala]] gain power in the Imperial Remnant for her own purposes. However, her dependency on avatars was ultimately her greatest weakness: killing any amount of avatar bodies in her possession also resulting in her strength weakening rapidly, to the point of "death" should all be destroyed, which Luke ultimately utilized to deliver the finishing blow on Abeloth in their duel. Also, she preferred to inhabit the bodies of Force-sensitives, as non Force-sensitives' bodies failed to last for long before deteriorating, and those born to two Force-Sensitive parents were more to her liking and seemed to last longer than those who had only one parent who could use the Force.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

[[File:The_Heart_of_the_Empire.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Abeloth fomented and fed on mass terror in the galactic capital.]]
Once [[Consume Essence|feeding on the suffering]] of Coruscant, her powers grew to the point she caused random lava flows by her mere presence and could have three manifestations at once.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> It was presumed she would become effectively all-powerful if allowed to feed on the suffering on Coruscant for long enough.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> She could make [[Sith shadow-ghoul|monsters]] appear from the bodies of the dead and could inhabit a computer. She even was able to resist a [[Force blast|Force Blast]] unleashed by [[Ben Skywalker]] in a state of [[Oneness/Legends|Oneness]] that could have knocked a frigate out of the [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] of a planet, though swiftly she was wounded by a thrown pillar--showing that her [[Force barrier/Legends|Force Barrier's]] power to block raw manifestations of the Force could be bypassed with thrown objects, much as what Skywalker's father did before to her.<ref name="Apocalypse" /><ref name="Vortex" /> Abeloth could used the bodies of slain Sith to summon Sith shadow-ghouls, monsters that could only be defeated by closing the eyelids of the host corpse. She also used [[Technometry]] and [[Flow-walking|Flow Walking]] in this state, though the latter power made her helpless while in the trance to use it.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> Her [[Force scream/Legends|Force Scream]] could stagger [[Jedi Master]]s.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> Abeloth was capable of producing a [[Force-flash]] that could affect the visuals of many ships in an entire star system, something that Luke Skywalker was not expected to be able to do.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

For all her power, even when boosted by the suffering of a whole world, she was not invincible as one of her manifestations was annihilated by a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|Thermal detonator]] and she would suffer wounds from blades, lightsabers, blasters, and Force-thrown objects that made it past her guard, though she was not always harmed as much as a mortal would be by such an attack.<ref name="Allies" /><ref name="Apocalypse" /><ref name="Vortex" /> Also, she was nearly overcome by Vol when she attacked his dreams and he fought back with [[Mind Shard]]s and [[Dun Möch/Legends|insults]].<ref name="Ascension" /> Moreover, [[Darth Krayt]] was able to harm her by draining her life force--though this hurt him and Luke just as much, and by recalling his severed hand that had lodged in her body in [[beyond shadows]]. This also made her ability to sustain her other acts lesser, such as how her ghouls were severely weakened after Krayt's attack.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> Despite these weaknesses, and the fact that each time a body died her power was reduced, she could not be truly slain except by the Mortis Dagger. Indeed, after her "destruction" at the hands of the Jedi and Sith, she was yet able to spawn a tentacle out of nowhere to briefly attack some Jedi, though this last known gasp of vengeance soon faded without killing anyone.<ref name="Vortex" /><ref name="Apocalypse" />

According to Vestara Khai, Abeloth may have, via unknown means, destroyed Sith shuttles.<ref name="Abyss" /> Abeloth was a masterful hand-to-hand combatant, surviving duels with some of the greatest warriors ever, often overcoming them with her tentacles.<ref name="Vortex" /><ref name="Apocalypse" />

Given the entity's power, Luke Skywalker was not surprised that Abeloth was able to [[Force stealth|conceal]] her Force presence when he led the Sith flotilla through the Maw, but without the tentacle presence that Ben Skywalker had used to pinpoint Sinkhole Station's location when they ventured there the first time.<ref name="Allies" /> Abeloth was able to endure many injuries. Ben Skywalker considered the Force lightning that Vestara Khai launched at Abeloth by the Font of Power to be enough to take down a [[Canderous-class assault tank|''Canderous''-class assault tank]], yet the entity was able to get back on her feet as soon as the attack stopped.<ref name="Apocalypse" />

==Equipment==
{{Expandsect}}
Abeloth controlled Ship, a sentient Sith Meditation Sphere who she used as a personal transport. In order to delay her pursuers, Abeloth left her world by sending Ship to take them to the Pool of Knowledge while she stole the Jedi's ''Horizon''-class star yacht ''Jade Shadow''.<ref name="Vortex" />

While on Pydyr as Callista Ming, Abeloth wore the sleeveless robe of a Fallanassi Adept.<ref name="Vortex" /> While on Nam Chorios as Ming, she had a lightsaber and wore somber robes befitting that of a Jedi Master and a pair of boots.<ref name="Conviction" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Conception and early development===
{{Quote|We developed the idea of a mysterious Force-entity locked in the Maw, who had come into contact with the young Jedi while they were being hidden from the Yuuzhan Vong at Shelter [in The New Jedi Order series]. By the next morning, we three writers were pretty confident that this was something we wanted to do, and we presented it to everyone else as an element about which we were all enthusiastic.|Troy Denning, on the making of Abeloth's character|<ref name="Apocalypse Now">{{InsiderCite|132|Apocalypse... Now!}}</ref>}}
[[File:FOTJ_poster.jpg|thumb|right|330px|Abeloth serves as the antagonist in the 2009&ndash;2012 series ''Fate of the Jedi''.]]
Abeloth was introduced as the primary antagonist in the nine-part ''[[Star Wars: Fate of the Jedi]]'' novel series, which was published between [[2009]] and [[2012]] and was authored by [[Aaron Allston]], [[Christie Golden]], and [[Troy Denning]], with the character debuting in the first novel, Allston's [[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast|''Outcast'']].<ref name="TERC" /> Abeloth was first identified by name in the third installment, 2009's [[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss|''Abyss'']], by Denning,<ref name="Abyss" /> and she was first pictured in a [[2011]] [[2011 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 6|''Topps Star Wars Galaxy'' Series 6]] trading card by [[Shea Standefer]], who sketched a tentacled figure in an undefined form.<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2011 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 6|cardname=Shea Standefer sketch cards}}</ref> The character was not depicted in [[Ian Keltie]]'s cover art for the novel series,<ref name="Apocalypse Now" /> and the following year's reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' includes the only other official illustration of Abeloth, made by [[Drew Baker]], depicting her Callista Ming avatar being attacked by the Jedi and the Sith.<ref name="Warfare" />

The concept of Abeloth as a mysterious and ancient being originated in<ref name="Apocalypse Now" /> a private meeting between Allston, Golden, and Denning at the latter's hotel room during the conceptualization stage of the ''Fate of the Jedi'' series,<ref name="Denning podcast" /> which editors [[Shelly Shapiro]] and [[Sue Rostoni]] set out as a joint journey of Luke and Ben Skywalker to investigate the cause of Jacen Solo's fall to the dark side&mdash;as shown in the preceding [[2006]]&ndash;[[2008]] novel series ''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]''&mdash;that is inspired by [[Wikipedia:Homer|Homer's]] [[Wikipedia:Ancient Greek literature|ancient Greek]] epic poem [[Wikipedia:Odyssey|''The Odyssey'']].<ref name="Apocalypse Now" /> The Mind Walkers drawn to Abeloth were inspired by ''The Odyssey''{{'s}} [[Wikipedia:Lotus-eaters|lotus-eaters]], and Callista Ming's return, absorbed by Abeloth, was mentioned in initial story discussions.<ref name="TERC" /> Denning considers Abeloth as a spiritual monster for a spiritual journey that organically developed from the personal and social journeys in the [[2005]] novel series ''[[Star Wars: The Dark Nest Trilogy]]'' and ''Legacy of the Force'', all involving Jacen Solo.<ref name="Suvudu">{{Suvudu|subdomain=star-wars|url=2012/03/interview-with-troy-denning-author-fate-of-the-jedi-apocalypse.html|text=Interview with Troy Denning, Author, "Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse"|author=Eric Geller|date=2012-03-20|nolive=1}}</ref>

[[File:Aaron_Allston.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Aaron Allston, author of ''Outcast'', ''Backlash'', and ''Conviction'']]
Aaron Allston proposed the idea of young Jedi becoming psychotic due to Abeloth and Chief of State Natasi Daala taking advantage of those troubles to banish Luke Skywalker, setting off his odyssey that is meant to be upbeat in contrast to the dark tone of ''Legacy of the Force''. Allston was also interested in exploring mysteries such as the Maw and the origins of Centerpoint Station. Abeloth was conceived as a nexus of dark side power that would tempt the Sith and provoke major turmoil without starting another war, but the idea that the Sith would be the One Sith featured in the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series, published by [[Dark Horse Comics]] between 2006 and [[2010]], was dropped when Dark Horse voiced discomfort with the novel series incorporating them. The ''Fate of the Jedi'' team therefore created a new group of Sith, the Lost Tribe of Sith, that worked with Abeloth,<ref name="Apocalypse Now" /> but they also included the One Sith in less prominent roles.<ref name="Apocalypse" /> Although Denning personally considers the Sith Lord who defeats Abeloth alongside Luke Skywalker to be a specific character appearing in subsequent stories, he wanted readers to come to their own interpretations individually; according to the 2012 reference title ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' by [[Pablo Hidalgo]], he is Darth Krayt.<ref name="TERC" /> ''Apocalypse''{{'s}} description of the Sith Lord matches Darth Krayt's features and ideals<ref name="Apocalypse" /> as shown in the ''Legacy'' comics.<ref name="Legacy 2006 15">[[Legacy (2006) 15|''Legacy'' (2006) 15]]</ref>

[[File:Christie-golden.jpg|thumb|right|240px|Christie Golden, author of ''Omen'', ''Allies'', and ''Ascension'']]
Christie Golden advocated the idea of pairing Ben Skywalker with a Sith&mdash;Vestara Khai&mdash;in the same vein as [[Wikipedia:William Shakespeare|William Shakespeare's]] play [[Wikipedia:Romeo and Juliet|''Romeo and Juliet'']];<ref name="Denning podcast" /> it would be used as a major element for characterization and plot development throughout the series. Similarly, Golden considers Abeloth to not only present a worthy foe to Luke Skywalker, but to attack his vulnerabilities given his characterization as someone who cares very deeply about others, considering the hurt of Callista Ming being used by Abeloth "uniquely villainous." Golden also joked that among the dropped ideas for ''Fate of the Jedi'' was Jaina Solo and Abeloth taking over the universe together while [[Pocket]], Wynn Dorvan's pet, becomes a Sith Lord.<ref name="Apocalypse Now" />

===Myths of Mortis===
{{Quote|She's beyond anything we can understand; we can understand a few things about her, but not everything. I really presented more facts about her history than I did about her powers or what her true nature is.|Troy Denning, regarding Abeloth|<ref name="Suvudu" />}}
[[File:Troydenning.jpg|thumb|left|230px|Troy Denning, author of ''Abyss'', ''Vortex'', and ''Apocalypse'']]
Denning introduced Abeloth in ''Abyss'' in a "Cthuloid" nature, borrowing from the [[Wikipedia:Cthulhu Mythos|mythology]] of [[Wikipedia:H. P. Lovecraft|H. P. Lovecraft's]] [[Wikipedia:Cthulhu|Cthulhu]].<ref name="Apocalypse Now" /> When Aaron Allston was asked whether Abeloth was inspired by the similarly named "[[w:c:forgottenrealms:Aboleth|aboleth]]" creatures of the [[w:c:forgottenrealms:Dungeons & Dragons|''Dungeons & Dragons'']] roleplaying game, he replied that he did not know her inspirations.<ref name="Aboleths">{{Suvudu|url=2011/06/interview-with-aaron-allston-author-star-wars-fate-of-the-jedi-conviction.html|text=Interview with Aaron Allston, Author, "Fate of the Jedi: Conviction"|author=Matt Staggs|date=2011-06-01|nolive=1}}</ref>

When the ''Fate of the Jedi'' team discussed tying Abeloth to the Celestials via email around the time of writing the<ref name="Suvudu" /> 2010<ref name="TERC" /> novels [[Fate of the Jedi: Allies|''Allies'']] and [[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex|''Vortex'']],<ref name="Suvudu" /> just after the release of [[Fate of the Jedi: Omen|''Omen'']]<ref name="Chee">{{WordPress|subdomain=roqoodepot|name=Roqoo Depot|url=interviews/leland-chee|text=Leland Chee|archivedate=20210513132544}}</ref> in 2009,<ref name="TERC" /> they were informed by [[Leland Chee]], who maintains the [[Holocron continuity database]], that the upcoming [[The Clone Wars: Season Three|third season]] of the television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', aired between 2010 and 2011, would include "some Celestial-stature characters." The ''Fate of the Jedi'' team thus coordinated with ''The Clone Wars'' showrunner [[Dave Filoni]], and Denning enjoyed listening to Filoni's thoughts on the Mortis episodes and how he generously helped the novelists to tie Abeloth to the Mortis myth.<ref name="Denning Filoni">{{WordPress|subdomain=roqoodepot|name=Roqoo Depot|url=2012/03/13/fotj-apocalypse-interview-with-troy-denning|text=&#8216;FOTJ: Apocalypse&#8217; Interview with Troy Denning|date=2012-03-13|archivedate=20210411222654}}</ref>

The authors initial idea was that Abeloth was a corrupted servant to the Celestials inhabiting the planet in the Maw, but the Celestials would not be showed as characters. After being put in contact with Filoni, the authors stopped short of calling the Ones in Mortis "Celestials,"<ref name="Suvudu" /> with Denning replying to a question about whether Abeloth was a Celestial that she was not, and that the Ones were what Celestials became&mdash;if one is to interpret the Killiks' claims<ref name="Denning Filoni" /> that he wrote in [[March]] 2012's [[Fate of the Jedi: Apocalypse|''Apocalypse'']]<ref name="Apocalypse" /> literally;<ref name="Denning Filoni" /> the ambiguity of the Killiks' accuracy regarding Abeloth's origins and the Celestial suited the purpose of the story to emphasise that they were beyond comprehension and elaborate on Abeloth's backstory while preserving the mystery of her powers and the true nature of her, Mortis, and the Celestials.<ref name="Suvudu" /> Denning also collaborated with [[Jason Fry]] in the latter's<ref name="Warfare Celestials" /> [[April]] 2012<ref name="WarfareDate">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/180097/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-star-wars-by-jason-fry-with-paul-r-urquhart/9780345477620|text=The Essential Guide to Warfare: Star Wars}}</ref> reference title, ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', co-authored with [[Paul R. Urquhart]], exploring the myth of the Celestials in the prologue chapter; it was cut from publication as editor [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] felt it did not suit the purpose of the book and instead released on [[StarWars.com]] on [[September 27]], 2013 as the first installment of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]].<ref name="Warfare Celestials" />

Abeloth's influence adapts continuity from the 2008 novel [[Millennium Falcon (novel)|''Millennium Falcon'']], written during the development of ''Fate of the Jedi'' by [[James Luceno]],<ref name="TERC" /> who also contributed to the series' brainstorming sessions,<ref name="Apocalypse" /> in which the Jedi Seff Hellin becomes psychotic and inquires about using YVH [[Battle droid/Legends|droids]] against Mandalorians;<ref name="MF" /> the cause of his psychosis was revealed to be Abeloth's influence in ''Abyss'',<ref name="Abyss" /> and a battle between YVHs and Mandalorians was incorporated in the [[2013]] novel [[Crucible (novel)|''Crucible'']],<ref name="Crucible" /> which was written by Denning for the [[original trilogy]]'s trio of Luke Skywalker, Leia Organa, and Han Solo to "pass the torch" to the next generation of heroes.<ref name="Denning podcast">{{WebCite|url=http://www.scumandvillainyradio.com/category/directory|text=Directory|work=Scum and Villainy Radio|archivedate=20140513074211}} {{C|BOMBAD EPISODE (EPISODE #18 FOR 3/28/2014)}}</ref> The author also consulted Dave Filoni via an intermediary about monoliths and the nature of the Force in the heroes' search for Mortis and its dagger, intended by the Jedi for an eventual "final showdown" with Abeloth, which Denning likened to the romantic quest for the [[Wikipedia:Holy Grail|Holy Grail]].<ref name="Denning Hollywood">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywood.com/movies/star-wars-crucible-troy-denning-interview-excerpt-55019540-60226140|text='Star Wars: Crucible': Troy Denning Talks Han, Luke, & Leia's 'Passing of the Torch,' Plus an Excerpt|date=2013-07-10|work=[https://www.hollywood.com Hollywood.com]|archivedate=20231220142730}}</ref>

The author considers the physical and spiritual wound that Abeloth left in Luke Skywalker to be a missing part of his Force-presence and an important weakness for further character development of him beyond ''Apocalypse''. Regarding Abeloth herself after her defeat, Denning personally considers her to be gone for "a couple of dozen millennia."<ref name="Denning Facebook">{{Facebook|username=troy.denning|url=starwarsbooks/posts/10150727438248713|name=[[Troy Denning]]|date=2012-04-04|quote=Toney, I do think that Luke has suffered a substantial physical and spiritual wound that should be reflected in future stories, but I don't know that it will keep him from playing a major part in future stories. (Again, I'm just the writer -- that really isn't my call). I think it should fall more into the category of a weakness that must be part of his arc in future stories. I like how you think of the wound, too -- part of his Force-presence missing. That's really what Abeloth did to him, isn't it<br />[&hellip;]<br />Jonothon -- I suppose there's a CHANCE that Abeloth could use Luke's wound to come back. But I honestly don't expect that to happen. Abeloth, in my mind at least, is gone for a couple of dozen millennia. Of course, I'm not the guy who determines future story arcs, so that's just my opinion.|archiveurl=https://archive.is/wip/detpL}}</ref> Following [[Lucasfilm]]'s creation of a new [[canon]] continuity in [[2014]], ''Crucible'' became chronologically the last novel of the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity.<ref name="Denning podcast" />
